parent_insertions.raw:
Realtime P3 metadata and protected transport prerequisites

The Realtime admission binary requires its own migrated `realtime_db`; the
Compose, DEV and staging migration catalogs include it. Staging/prod examples
reference `REALTIME_DATABASE_URL`. Provision the database/login and restoreable
backup using the existing environment process before upgrading the binary;
configuration changes alone are not migration or rollout evidence.

The deployment templates require these environment-scoped external assets:
`voice-realtime-principal-signing` (only `current.pem`, `next.pem`, PKCS#8),
`voice-p3-principal-public` (public `realtime.json` derived from exactly that
generation), `voice-realtime-p3-tls`, `voice-chat-realtime-p3-tls`,
`voice-p3-principal-jwks-tls`, `voice-p3-principal-replay` (`password`) and
`voice-p3-principal-trust` (`chat-server-ca.crt`, `space-client-ca.crt`,
`space-jwks-ca.crt`, `realtime-client-ca.crt`, `realtime-jwks-ca.crt`). Consumer
mounts project only their trust roots; private signer keys mount only in Realtime.
The independent publisher mounts the public document and its own HTTPS identity,
never issuer keys. Its TCP probe is transport availability only; Chat verifies
the HTTPS issuer set before serving its native resolver. Certificate SANs match
the exact service DNS configured in the templates; the Realtime leaf supports
outbound client authentication as well as its protected Space server identity.
No real secret material is committed or generated by deployment templates.

Local Compose derives public Space/Realtime sets in its existing isolated
initializer before starting their independent HTTPS publisher. Existing partial
or old principal volumes fail closed. Do not reset shared volumes or overwrite
identities: reconcile an owned stopped project, preserve database/admission/
terminal-fence state, and prepare a scoped replacement principal generation.
Static publication supports a switch to an already published next signing key;
hot key replacement needs a separate coherent generation and overlap procedure.
Phase0's opt-in overlay consumes the actual fixture Space issuer instead of the
base initializer's distinct Space keys. This does not qualify whole-stack startup.

Global P3 activation remains separate: prove every old/new writer covered or
terminated, all eleven participants present, metadata restored safely, and a
qualified recovery/rollback package. This implementation supports cooperative
closure only. A dead incarnation with unresolved admissions stays pending;
neither timeout nor an operator boolean settles it. Rollback must preserve these
tickets and permanent denies and cannot reintroduce an unguarded older writer.
Shared DEV/STAGING operations still require the current TT resource protocol;
these source templates do not claim a stand or appoint a tester.

##

Owner capability policy

The [runtime capability contract](testing/release-capability-runtime-contract.md)
defines the immutable v2 policy, owner guards, effective snapshot and qualification
boundary. Notification now consumes that policy at bootstrap and its final push
boundary. Its alpha image needs independently bound compiled source, mounted
policy/digest and a private fresh snapshot target before rollout. Legacy configs
do not qualify; all other owners, full negative runners and deployment acceptance
remain required. The local Compose Notification fixture explicitly uses the
nonqualifying development profile.
